case_title: Raju and Another v. State of Uttarakhand
high_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused were involved in an altercation with the victims, who were friends of the complainant. The complainant's son and his friends returned from a cinema and encountered the accused near a house. The accused were armed with knives and lathis. The victims were assaulted, and the accused fled. The complainant later filed an FIR based on the account of his son and his friends. The investigation led to charges under Section 307 of the IPC. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court convicted two of them. The Supreme Court reviewed the evidence, noting inconsistencies in witness testimonies, medical reports, and the FIR, which was filed by a hearsay witness. The court found the prosecution's case incomplete and the acquittal by the trial court to be well-reasoned.
